patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient has been experiencing tingling pain in the sole of his right foot for the last 6 weeks, which occurs when he raises his foot above chest level during exercises. He started exercising regularly 2 months ago and notices his right calf cramps when using the incline feature on his treadmill, requiring him to stop frequently. The pain subsides after a few minutes of rest. He has been managing type 2 diabetes mellitus for 8 years. He is a smoker with a 34-year history of smoking two packs per day.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Tingling pain in the sole of the right foot during exercise
Secondary_Symptoms: Right calf cramps with incline exercise

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: Type 2 diabetes mellitus, managed with metformin for the past 8 years.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Smoking history of two packs per day for 34 years.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate a 55-year-old man presenting with foot pain and cramping during exercise, and diagnose the underlying condition.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “Lately I’ve had a tingling pain on the sole of my right foot for about six weeks, especially when I lift my foot higher during exercises. Also, when I use the incline on the treadmill my right calf starts cramping and I have to stop, but the pain goes away after a few minutes of rest.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or the whites of your eyes?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any yellowing of my skin or in the whites of my eyes.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you feel stiffness in your joints when you wake up in the morning? If yes, does it usually improve after you start moving around?
turns.patient_answer: “No—when I wake up I don’t feel joint stiffness, and I don’t notice it improving once I start moving around.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling confused lately—like you’re having trouble thinking clearly, staying oriented, or recognizing where you are or what’s going on?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t been confused or having trouble thinking clearly, staying oriented, or recognizing where I am.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been having **night sweats**—waking up during the night drenched in sweat or needing to change clothes or bed sheets?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had night sweats or been waking up drenched enough to change my clothes or bed sheets.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed a lump or swelling in your thigh that feels like it’s within the muscle (not just on the skin)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any lump or swelling in my thigh that feels like it’s within the muscle. I mainly just get tingling in the sole of my right foot with the exercise, and my right calf cramps when I use the treadmill incline.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any skin lesions, bumps, or sores that seem to follow or line up along the veins on your arm (for example, along the inner arm or where the veins are more visible)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any skin lesions, bumps, or sores along the veins on my arms, and I don’t see anything lining up where the veins are more visible.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you worked in an environment where you might breathe in metal dust or metal fumes—for example welding, grinding, cutting, machining, construction/renovation with metal, battery work, or working with metal powders? (Yes or no)
turns.patient_answer: “No—nothing like welding, grinding, cutting, or working around metal dust or fumes; I haven’t had any battery work or metal powder exposure either.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any swelling or enlargement around a joint that feels bony or hard (for example in the fingers, knuckles, knees, or hips)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any swelling or enlargement around any joints like the knuckles, knees, or hips—nothing feels bony or hard.”

turns.doctor_question: I’m sorry you’re dealing with this. **Do you have pain in your thigh right now** (yes or no)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I don’t have pain in my thigh right now. My symptoms are mainly the tingling in the sole of my right foot during exercise and the right calf cramps when I use the incline—then it settles after a few minutes of rest.”

turns.doctor_question: I’m sorry you’re dealing with this—can I ask: **do you experience pain or discomfort during sex (either at the entrance or deeper inside)?**
turns.patient_answer: “No, I don’t experience pain or discomfort during sex.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any scattered skin lesions—like small bumps, spots, or sores—appearing in different areas of your body?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any scattered skin lesions, small bumps, spots, or sores appearing in different areas of my body.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that you (or the person you’re caring for) seem unusually restless, irritable, or unable to stay calm—more than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed being unusually restless, irritable, or unable to stay calm—my mood and behavior feel about the same as usual.”

turns.doctor_question: I’m sorry you’re dealing with this. To check for something important: **are you having chest pain right now** (yes or no)?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I’m not having chest pain right now.”
